> This is my first stage in building my Pico BOT!!! First I have to start with the face. I use 4 MAX7219 Dot Matrix Display Modules to create 2 eyes and a mouth for my robot. I'm displaying this face with a sequence of facial expressions such as sadFace() or angryFace(). I built a CAD design based off the M.A.X robot from Meccano as well!

## Design

### 2026-11-01: ##Matrix Design #1 of Pico Head

**5.77h**

##Matrix Design #1 of Pico Head

note to half life: I did not record any coding hours in this timelapse.

I spent time researching how to use the ```LedControl.h``` library and found the main way to actually display images is through bytes. For example:
```
byte eyeBlink[8] = {
  0b00000000,
  0b00000000,
  0b00000000,
  0b11111111,
  0b11111111,
  0b00000000,
  0b00000000,
  0b00000000
};
```

As I haven't used Led matrixes before I wasn't sure if my code was working hardware wise, I tried using "Tinkercad" or a new website I found called "benchtwin.com" but it was hard finding the right MAX7219 Module. Eventually I decided to trust that my code would work as intended on the Led Matrix and debug when my parts arrive. To help me plan out where I would switch LEDs on and off, I made a whiteboard on Canva and pasted in an array of dots and worked from there. I spent some time finding the configuration I liked for each  face expression. These expressions helped me draw out each look with bytes. I also added a DHT11 and photoresistor so the face could react to some inputs.

![LEDMATRIX](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/eP8CGAI2wXebtYyMKgVtSC7r0m8Quc3O/ff18ccda6cb64d6893dadb6e30304197ee4d189d7aa38c3fd1297bf00a2a98ca.png)

## PICO CAD 2

I spent most of this time working out the front part of the module, with a little curved overhang at the top. I based my design of the Meccano M.A.X robot and extended it to fit 4 Matrix Modules.  I built this by taking rough measurements from my disassembled M.A.X robot as a guide and scaled them appropriately.

![meccano-m-a-x-17401](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/eP8CGAI2wXebtYyMKgVtSC7r0m8Quc3O/2a2f681f5782204c7e856e02ba95bfec1f98e0dc852122ceba6644aa1809c8e7.jpg)

## Final Look At PICO's Face!!

I added holes at the front of PICO's face to thread screws into, the measurements I took were from the manufacturer. I added a small tab at the back of the face so the front and side piece snaps together nicely. I built the side piece by creating a quick sketch with lines and dimensioning according to my first piece, then offset the sketch by 3-4mm. Extruding the sketch got the me the sides I wanted, I then added some holes around each wall to save print time and look a little cooler too. I added a top layer where I would be able to wire and place my electronics on with holes for wires to go through all around the project.
